deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a draft of the opening of Riemann's 1857 fragment on n-valued systems of functions with prescribed branch points and constant linear monodromy. It was published posthumously in the Werke (1876) as 'Zwei allgemeine Lehrsätze über lineare Differentialgleichungen mit algebraischen Coefficienten'. The previous page defines systems y = (y_1..y_n) that are single-valued except at branch points a, b, ..., g. A positive loop around a sends y to A·y, and the monodromy matrices satisfy G···B·A = 1. Assuming A has distinct eigenvalues, it is diagonalized as A = α·diag(λ_1..λ_n)·α^{-1}.

Step 1 (top lines). The diagonalizing substitution α is not unique. Riemann notes that, apart from the equation determining it (the eigenvalue condition), it can contain arbitrary values. Any nonzero determinant is allowed, i.e. the eigenvector columns can be rescaled (my reading of the cramped lines).

Step 2. Put z = α^{-1} y. A loop around a sends y to A y. Hence z goes to α^{-1} A y = α^{-1} α Λ α^{-1} y = Λ z. So (z_1..z_n) goes to (λ_1 z_1, ..., λ_n z_n). Each z_i is therefore multiplicatively multivalued around a.

Step 3. Suppose a function z acquires the factor λ under a positive loop around a. Since (x-a)^μ acquires e^{2πiμ}, choose μ = log λ/(2πi). Then z·(x-a)^{-μ} is single-valued in a punctured neighbourhood of a and has a Laurent expansion in integer powers of (x-a). Hence z_i expands in powers (x-a)^{log λ_i/(2πi) + m}, with m an integer.

Step 4. Hypothesis: the z are nowhere infinite of infinitely high order (no essential singularities, i.e. moderate growth / regular singularity). Then each series terminates on the side of decreasing powers. Let μ_i be the lowest exponent, so z_i (x-a)^{-μ_i} is finite and nonzero at x = a. The analogous exponents at b, ..., g are ν_i, ..., ς_i.

Step 5. For two systems of the same class (same branch points and same monodromy), the λ_i are fixed by (A). Because they are distinct, exponents can be matched unambiguously, and corresponding exponents differ only by integers. So the integer parts of the exponents distinguish systems within a class.

Step 6. Riemann therefore uses as the characteristic of a system the symbol P{a b ... g; (A) (B) ... (G); μ_1 ν_1 ... ς_1; ...; μ_n ν_n ... ς_n}(x). This is the n-dimensional generalization of his 1857 P-function symbol, with exponents attached to each branch point.

Step 7 (announced, proved on the next page). Between any n+1 systems of the same class there is a linear homogeneous relation whose coefficients are polynomials in x. The next page proves it via the n×n minors of the n×(n+1) matrix: they acquire the factor det(A), and their lowest exponents are controlled by sums of the μ's. It then derives that y satisfies an nth-order linear ODE with polynomial (rational) coefficients.
errors: The substitution z = (α)^{-1} y is written in the transcription as (A)^{-1}, and the image (A)^{-1}(A)y as well. It must be (α)^{-1} and (α)^{-1}(A)(y) = Λ(α)^{-1}(y). This is most likely a transcription confusion between α and A; otherwise it is a slip.

Unjustified as stated: the claim that corresponding exponents of two systems in a class differ by integers also tacitly needs the diagonalizing bases to be matched. These bases differ by diagonal rescaling, and by permutation of equal-λ blocks, which is excluded by the distinct-eigenvalue assumption. This is fine under Riemann's stated restriction.
The theorem on n+1 systems is only announced here; the proof (next page) also needs control at x = ∞, which is not on this page.

results.what: Diagonalization of a monodromy matrix A = α Λ α^{-1}; the transformed functions z = α^{-1} y are multiplied by λ_i under a loop
results.modern_name: Local monodromy diagonalization / eigenbasis of local monodromy
results.usually_credited_to: Linear algebra (Cauchy, Weierstrass, Jordan); in the ODE context Fuchs 1866 and Riemann 1857 (published 1876)

results.what: z(x-a)^{-log λ/2πi} is single-valued near a; with the no-essential-singularity hypothesis, local expansions start at finite exponents μ_i ≡ log λ_i/(2πi) mod 1
results.modern_name: Local exponents at a regular singular point (indicial exponents); moderate growth condition

results.what: Generalized P-symbol listing branch points, monodromy matrices and exponents; systems of the same class distinguished by integer shifts of exponents
results.modern_name: Riemann scheme / Riemann P-symbol for rank-n local systems; Riemann–Hilbert data

results.what: Any n+1 systems of the same class satisfy a linear homogeneous relation with polynomial coefficients
results.modern_name: Rank-n local system over C(x); module of multivalued sections with given monodromy has rank n; leads to the Fuchsian ODE realizing given monodromy

deep.surprise_reason: This page is a draft of Riemann's well-known 1857 fragment 'Zwei allgemeine Lehrsätze über lineare Differentialgleichungen mit algebraischen Coefficienten', published in the Werke (1876). The diagonalization, local exponents, P-scheme and the n+1-systems theorem are all already attributed to him. It is a draft variant of known material.

checkable.asserts: (x-a)^mu acquires exactly the factor lambda under a positive loop when mu = log(lambda)/(2*pi*i)
z*(x-a)^(-mu) is single-valued: the factors lambda and exp(-2*pi*i*mu) cancel

checkable.sympy: A = Matrix([[2,1],[0,3]]); P, D = A.diagonalize(); simplify(P.inv()*A*P - D) == zeros(2)
checkable.asserts: A matrix with distinct eigenvalues is diagonalized as alpha^{-1} A alpha = Lambda, i.e. z = alpha^{-1} y transforms as z -> Lambda z

checkable.sympy: A = Matrix([[2,1],[0,3]]); P, D = A.diagonalize(); S = diag(5,7); simplify((P*S).inv()*A*(P*S) - D) == zeros(2)
checkable.asserts: The diagonalizing alpha is determined only up to diagonal rescaling (arbitrary nonzero constants), as Riemann remarks

checkable.sympy: mu1 = Rational(1,3); mu2 = mu1 + 2; simplify(exp(2*pi*I*mu1) - exp(2*pi*I*mu2)) == 0
checkable.asserts: Exponents differing by integers give the same monodromy factor, so systems in the same class can differ by integer shifts of exponents

transcription_corrections: '(A)^{-1}(y_1, y_2, ..., y_n)' should read '(α)^{-1}(y_1, ..., y_n)', i.e. the diagonalizing substitution, not the monodromy A.
'A.(z_1, z_2, ..., z_n) = ...' is likely 'Ist (z_1, ..., z_n) = (α)^{-1}(y)' or 'Die ... (z)'; the leading 'A.' is probably a misread.
'mit ganzen [-rationalen-] Coefficienten': the image shows 'mit ganzen rationalen' struck, with the coefficients 'die ganze Functionen von x sind'.
In the P-symbol the second row is (A) (B) ... (G) (monodromy matrices), followed by exponent rows μ_i, ν_i, ..., ς_i (the last column letter resembles ς or σ).
The opening line '𝔣)' and 'dass er bei der Zerlegung der Substitution ...' are uncertain; the sense is a remark about the non-uniqueness of the diagonalizing substitution α.
